title: My robot stopped moving
description: A drive controller is listening, but nobody is sending velocity commands.
text:
Symptom: The robot stopped moving after restarting navigation. ROS2 Humble, differential drive.

$ ros2 topic list
/cmd_vel
/odom
/scan
/tf
/tf_static

$ ros2 node list
/controller_server
/planner_server
/bt_navigator
/diff_drive_controller

$ ros2 topic info /cmd_vel
Type: geometry_msgs/msg/Twist
Publisher count: 0
Subscription count: 1

$ ros2 node info /diff_drive_controller
Subscribers:
  /cmd_vel: geometry_msgs/msg/Twist
Publishers:
  /odom: nav_msgs/msg/Odometry

$ ros2 lifecycle get /controller_server
inactive [2]

[bt_navigator] Waiting for navigation goal.
[controller_server] Configured controller FollowPath.
[controller_server] Waiting for lifecycle activation.

Question: Why does /cmd_vel exist but the robot does not move?

title: Odometry went quiet
description: Navigation has not received fresh odometry for 8.4 seconds.
text:
Symptom: Navigation pauses while driving. ROS2 Humble.

$ ros2 topic info /odom
Type: nav_msgs/msg/Odometry
Publisher count: 1
Subscription count: 2

$ ros2 topic hz /odom
No messages received for 8.4 seconds

[controller_server] /odom stale: last update was 8.4 seconds ago.
[diff_drive_controller] Waiting for wheel state updates.

title: A disconnected TF tree
description: The laser frame cannot connect to the robot base.
text:
Symptom: Laser scan does not appear in RViz. ROS2 Humble.

[rviz2] Could not find a connection between 'base_link' and 'laser' because they are not part of the same tree.

$ ros2 topic echo /scan --once
header:
  frame_id: laser
angle_min: -3.14
angle_max: 3.14

URDF excerpt:
<link name="base_link"/>
<link name="laser_link"/>
<joint name="laser_joint" type="fixed">
  <parent link="base_link"/>
  <child link="laser_link"/>
  <origin xyz="0.2 0 0.15" rpy="0 0 0"/>
</joint>

title: LiDAR is not publishing
description: A scan subscriber is waiting for a missing sensor driver.
text:
Symptom: Costmap is empty and no scan is visible. ROS2 Humble.

$ ros2 topic info /scan
Type: sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan
Publisher count: 0
Subscription count: 1

$ ros2 topic echo /scan
WARNING: topic [/scan] does not appear to be published yet

[lidar_driver] Failed to open serial port /dev/ttyUSB0: Permission denied
[lidar_driver] Shutting down driver.

title: One parameter, one crashed node
description: A YAML string is supplied where the node expects a number.
text:
Symptom: The drive node exits during launch. ROS2 Humble.

[drive_node] rclpy.exceptions.InvalidParameterTypeException: Trying to set parameter 'wheel_radius' to '0.033' of type STRING, expecting type DOUBLE
[ERROR] [drive_node]: process has died [exit code 1].

params.yaml:
drive_node:
  ros__parameters:
    wheel_radius: "0.033"
    wheel_separation: 0.16

Node source excerpt:
self.declare_parameter('wheel_radius', 0.033)

title: Navigation cannot find the map
description: The map → odom transform is unavailable to Nav2.
text:
Symptom: Nav2 global costmap does not initialize. ROS2 Humble.

[global_costmap] Timed out waiting for transform from base_link to map.
[global_costmap] Invalid frame ID "map" passed to canTransform: frame does not exist
[bt_navigator] map -> odom transform missing

$ ros2 node list
/map_server
/amcl
/controller_server
/robot_state_publisher

$ ros2 lifecycle get /amcl
inactive [2]

$ ros2 run tf2_ros tf2_echo odom base_link
At time 1712345678.0
Translation: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

title: Same topic, incompatible QoS
description: The scan publisher and subscriber disagree on reliability.
text:
Symptom: /scan has a publisher, but my subscriber receives nothing. ROS2 Humble.

$ ros2 topic info /scan --verbose
Type: sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan
Publisher count: 1
Subscription count: 1
Node name: lidar_driver
Endpoint type: PUBLISHER
QoS profile:
  Reliability: BEST_EFFORT
  Durability: VOLATILE
Node name: obstacle_monitor
Endpoint type: SUBSCRIPTION
QoS profile:
  Reliability: RELIABLE
  Durability: VOLATILE

[obstacle_monitor] New publisher discovered on topic '/scan', offering incompatible QoS. No messages will be received from it. Last incompatible policy: RELIABILITY

title: Python cannot find a module
description: The active interpreter cannot import a dependency.
text:
$ python robot.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "robot.py", line 2, in <module>
    import serial
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'serial'

title: A Python runtime exception
description: An empty sensor sample list breaks an average calculation.
text:
$ python monitor.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "monitor.py", line 18, in <module>
    average = sum(samples) / len(samples)
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

Relevant source:
samples = []
average = sum(samples) / len(samples)
